name: rankine_cycle_part_load
title: Rankine cycle with cooling-water condenser, generator/motor and part load
summary: Superheated-steam Rankine cycle after the TESPy basic tutorial: steam turbine, feed pump, steam generator with pressure drop and main condenser cooled by a cooling-water stream, with generator and pump-motor efficiencies; a second, simultaneous block solves one part-load point where Stodola's cone law sets the turbine inlet pressure and the condenser UA and the cooling-water volumetric flow keep their design values.

authors: Francesco Witte (TESPy lead developer) and the TESPy contributors

verification.summary: Compared with a re-run of the TESPy tutorial rankine.py: design point 22 variables, max 2.9e-12; part-load point at 15 kg/s 13 variables, max 2.8e-11; the part-load sweep agrees to <= 1e-8 and the specification variants to round-off.
verification.reference: TESPy tutorial rankine.py re-run from the local snapshot (commit 19425523) in a throw-away venv (Python 3.12, CoolProp 8.1.0), with the plotting blocks removed and c2.set_attr(design=['p']) added to the sec_9 block; compared with tools/compare_solution.py: design point (22 variables, max 2.9e-12), part-load point at 15 kg/s (13 variables, max 2.8e-11), part-load sweep 20-10 kg/s (<= 1e-8), ttd_u = 4 K and net-power 10 MW variants (round-off)
verification.notes: TESPy stores no numbers for this tutorial, so the script itself was re-run (plotting libraries are not installed in the venv; the physics is untouched). Same CoolProp equation of state on both sides. The part-load design point is the base case of the model (m = 10 kg/s, p_2 = 0.1 bar) rather than the 20 kg/s / ttd_u state of sec_10; the TESPy re-run was adapted to the same reference point. The inventory note of TSP-034 quotes x_out = 0.866 from an independent CoolProp 7.2 check; TESPy (CoolProp 8.1.0) and CoolSolve give 0.86546.
